hints: Focus on adding up the atomic numbers of all the atoms, then adjust for the charge to get total electrons.
Try counting for $\text{ClO}_4^-$ first, $17 + (4 \times 8) + 1$ gives you a key number to compare against.
Check the telluride ion last and see if its total, starting from tellurium with atomic number 52, matches the 50 electron pattern of the others.
walkthrough:
**Remember the Electron Counting Rule**

Great start, this is just book-keeping. Total electrons equals the sum of atomic numbers plus extra electrons for negative charge, or minus electrons for positive charge.

$$\text{total } e^- = \sum (\text{atomic numbers}) + \text{charge magnitude for anions}$$

**Count Electrons in A, B and C**

Let us work them out together, they all look different but watch what happens. Use $\text{H}=1$, $\text{O}=8$, $\text{S}=16$, $\text{Cl}=17$.

$$\text{A: ClO}_4^- = 17 + (4 \times 8) + 1 = 50$$
$$\text{B: H}_2\text{SO}_4 = (2 \times 1) + 16 + (4 \times 8) = 50$$
$$\text{C: SO}_4^{2-} = 16 + (4 \times 8) + 2 = 50$$

**Count Electrons in Telluride and Decide**

Now for tellurium, atomic number 52, with a 2- charge we add two more electrons. That gives a clearly different total.

$$\text{D: Te}^{2-} = 52 + 2 = 54$$
Three species have 50 electrons and are isoelectronic, while one has 54.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{ClO}_4^-$ has $17 + 32 + 1 = 50$ electrons, so it matches B and C. Students sometimes forget to add 1 for the 1- charge.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is neutral so no charge adjustment is needed, $2 + 16 + 32 = 50$ electrons. It is isoelectronic with A and C.
options.C: Incorrect. $\text{SO}_4^{2-}$ has $16 + 32 + 2 = 50$ electrons, the same as A and B. A common slip is to add only 1 instead of 2 for the 2- charge.
options.D: Correct. $\text{Te}^{2-}$ has atomic number 52 plus 2 for the charge, giving 54 electrons. This is 4 more than the 50 electrons found in each of the other three species.
